chunks: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
One who fixes the time for you among the people, do not hesitate to call him a liar, for we do not specify a time for anyone.

key_terms.وَقَتَ: to fix or specify a time

ai.seo_question: What should one do if someone claims to know the exact time of the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) establishes the principle of 'ta'wil' (interpretive flexibility) regarding the Imam's return, noting that while the Imams knew the time, they did not fix it for public disclosure to prevent premature expectations. This teaching underscores the Shia doctrine that the exact hour is known only to Allah, distinguishing between divine knowledge and human speculation. It serves as a critical counter to those who claim definitive knowledge of the Mahdi's arrival date.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 414 - It is narrated from Fadhl bin Shazan from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan bin Yahya from Abu Ayyub Kharraz from Muhammad bin Muslim from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said: “
One who fixes the time of reappearance for you, do not pay attention to his falsification, because we have not specified its time for anyone.”
